item.title: ⟡ Winter sun, from our own local airport
item.description:
⟡ Winter sun, from our own local airport
A winter holiday feels different when it starts close to home.
This winter you can fly from Bournemouth to Madeira, Tenerife and the rest of the Canaries, Malta and Malaga, with no long drive to Gatwick and no dark start on the motorway.
We love that. It makes a week of sunshine in January feel so much easier to say yes to.
And once the flight's sorted, the lovely part begins. Choosing where you'll stay, from afternoon tea at Reid's Palace in Funchal to a Tenerife hotel that looks out across the water to La Gomera.
We've put together where you can fly this winter, and next summer too, in our latest journal piece.
Whenever you're ready to plan it, we'd love to help.
Come find us at No.82.
🕶️ ✉️ hello@agentnouveau.com

item.title: ⟡ A few special winter trips from Bournemouth
item.description:
⟡ A few special winter trips from Bournemouth
If you've a little one counting down to Christmas, Bournemouth has a few lovely surprises for you this winter.
In December there are Lapland trips from right here, a day trip to Enontekiö and short breaks to Ivalo. Snow under the pines, cold air on your cheeks and a little one who can't stop talking about Santa, all without a long drive first.
For the grown-ups, there's a single trip to Reykjavík in February, and in January a charter flight to Barbados that comes with a Caribbean cruise on P&O's Britannia.
They're special trips rather than regular routes, and that's a big part of what makes them feel special.
If one of them has caught your eye, come and talk it through with us. We've written them all up in our journal, alongside our other winter favourites from Bournemouth.
Come find us at No.82.
🕶️ ✉️ hello@agentnouveau.com

item.title: ⟡ Next summer, Greece from Bournemouth
item.description:
⟡ Next summer, Greece from Bournemouth
Next summer, Corfu, Kos and Crete are all a direct flight from Bournemouth, and that makes us very happy.
It means the Greek holiday you've been thinking about can start close to home. Lavender and butterflies at Ikos Kissamos in west Crete. A little Onassis history at Domes Miramare on Corfu. That's where our minds wander first.
If Greece is calling, our Ikos Supper Club would be a lovely place to begin. Ikos has resorts on Corfu, Kos and Crete, and we'd love you to spend the evening with us.
Ikos Supper Club · Thursday 22 October · No.82 Poole Road, Westbourne
Our favourite flights from Bournemouth next summer are in our latest journal piece.

item.title: CORI Hornbæk (Mon 19 Oct)
item.description:
Destination Spotlight: Hornbæk has a new little hotel by the harbour, and you can walk straight out onto the beach.
CORI Hornbæk opened this September, up on the Danish coast north of Copenhagen.
Your morning starts at The Jetty with an espresso, and by evening the same bar is shaking cocktails. In between, there's CORI Table, cooking with whatever's local and in season.
October suits it. The beach empties out, the wind comes in off the sea, and a walk through the woods of Hornbæk Plantage feels like just the thing before dinner.
There's a spa on the way in November, too.
It sits beautifully at the end of a few days in Copenhagen, and we'd love to put the two together for you.
Come find us at No.82. 🕶️ ✉️ hello@agentnouveau.com

item.title: Isle of Mull (Tue 20 Oct)
item.description:
Mull in October is a treat, and you'll see why the moment you step off the ferry.
The ferries from Oban run through the day. Then there's Duart Castle guarding the sea cliffs, single-track roads winding round the coast, and Tobermory with its bright row of coloured houses along the harbour.
It's an island for eating well. A plate of seafood at The Creel, and afternoons that stretch on a little longer than you meant them to.
On 23 and 24 October, Tobermory hosts its book festival, which feels like exactly the right excuse for a long weekend.
While you're there, the sky's worth watching. Eagles soar along this coast, and if you're lucky, there are otters on the shore.
Tell us when you'd like to go, and we'll take care of the ferries.

item.title: Sage Lodge (Wed 21 Oct)
item.description:
Destination Spotlight: your fire is lit, the river's outside, and Sage Lodge has three MICHELIN Keys for the third year running.
The lodge sits on the banks of the Yellowstone River in Montana, about 35 minutes north of Yellowstone National Park.
Out here, the days are simple. You can cast a line on the Yellowstone, float the river through Paradise Valley, or simply walk out and keep going.
After dinner at The Grill, there's the fire, a last glass and the hills going dark outside the window.
It's a wonderful base for Yellowstone, with somewhere special to come back to after your days in the park.
Come find us at No.82. 🕶️ ✉️ hello@agentnouveau.com

item.title: Queenstown and the Routeburn (Thu 22 Oct)
item.description:
From 1 November, New Zealand's Great Walks season opens again, and if you love a walk in the mountains, the Routeburn is a beauty.
It starts outside Glenorchy, at the head of Lake Wakatipu, and most people take three days over it. You climb through forest and past waterfalls to Harris Saddle, then down to Lake Mackenzie, where you sleep with the mountains all around you.
We love giving you a few days in Queenstown first, so you start the walk rested. Kayaking on the lake, a drive out through the Kawarau Gorge, dinner by the water with the Remarkables across the lake.
November is spring there, a beautiful time to walk, and we'll gladly put the days together for you.

item.title: Belmond La Samanna (Fri 23 Oct)
item.description:
Destination Spotlight: you can be back on Baie Longue from 15 November, when La Samanna opens for the season.
Belmond La Samanna sits on the cliffs above Baie Longue on St Martin, with white villas, lush gardens and the Caribbean right there below.
It's a place for long, unhurried days. A morning swim, a cabana on the beach, lunch at La Spiaggia with your book beside you.
In the evening, there's L'Oursin, with cooking from France and a little of the Caribbean in it, and a sunset over the water to finish the day.
What we love most is lunch running on into the afternoon, with nobody checking the time.
Longing for somewhere warm this winter? Baie Longue is where we'd start you off.

item.title: Volcanoes National Park, Rwanda (Sat 24 Oct)
item.description:
You set off early, with mist still hanging over the Virunga volcanoes, knowing there's a family of mountain gorillas somewhere up ahead.
Volcanoes National Park in northern Rwanda covers five of the Virunga volcanoes, with bamboo forest on their slopes and a green crater lake at the top of Bisoke.
Dian Fossey wrote that up here you shiver more than you sweat, and the air is cool and fresh. But when you finally see the gorillas, going about their morning as though you aren't there at all, nobody is thinking about the cold.
There are golden monkeys in the bamboo too, and a hike up to that crater lake if you'd like one more day.
Years later, you'll still be talking about that first hour with the gorillas.
Whenever you feel ready, we'll plan it with you, one slow morning at a time.
Come find us at No.82. 🕶️ ✉️ hello@agentnouveau.com

item.title: Cora Cora Maldives (Fri 9 Oct)
item.description:
Destination Spotlight: Cora Cora has just turned five, and you'll find it back open just in time for its birthday.
The island in Raa Atoll closed for a few weeks this summer for a little care and attention, then opened again at the end of September, ready for 1 October.
It's all-inclusive, which we love for a Maldives stay. You stop doing sums and start saying yes.
Lunch might be at Acquapazza on the beach. Dinner could be teppanyaki at Teien, or a slow evening of Spice Route flavours at Tazäa. And if you're travelling as a family, there's a lagoon pool villa with its own slide, which tends to settle who gets which room.
If the Maldives is on your wish list this winter, we'd love to talk it through with you.

item.title: Lahemaa, Estonia (Sat 10 Oct)
item.description:
You're walking a wooden boardwalk across Viru bog, with dark, still pools on either side of you.
This is Lahemaa, about an hour from Tallinn along the southern shore of the Gulf of Finland, and autumn suits it beautifully. The bog turns rust and gold, the forest smells of pine, and the coast is scattered with huge boulders the glaciers left behind after the last Ice Age. Few places in Europe have more of them.
Then there are the old manor houses. Palmse, Sagadi, Vihula, Kolga… each one a little different, and lovely to wander round on a grey afternoon.
Lynx, bears and beavers live out in the forest too. Seeing one would take real luck, but it's rather nice knowing they're there.
Tallinn with a couple of days in Lahemaa makes a lovely autumn break, and we'd happily put one together for you.

item.title: Dromoland Castle (Mon 12 Oct)
item.description:
Destination Spotlight: you'll find Dromoland at its loveliest this autumn, just before it closes for a while.
The castle in County Clare, once the ancestral home of the O'Brien family, closes in November for a big transformation and won't welcome guests again until the summer of 2027.
When it does, there'll be more rooms, a glass atrium at its heart and saunas looking out over Lough Dromoland.
But there's something lovely about catching it before all that. An afternoon in the drawing room. A walk through the walled gardens with the leaves coming down. A row out on the lake before dinner, with the castle standing over the water behind you.
It's a 500-acre estate, so there's plenty of room to wander, and the days take care of themselves.
It would be a pleasure to find you a few autumn nights there before the doors close.

item.title: The Wachau (Tue 13 Oct)
item.description:
We're dreaming of the Wachau this morning, and of you walking up through the vines as the fog lifts off the Danube.
This little stretch of the Danube valley in Austria is at its best in October. The harvest is coming in, the steep vineyards are turning gold, and the whole valley slows right down.
You can walk a stretch of the World Heritage Trail through the vines at Weißenkirchen, look down on the river, then find a wine tavern for a glass of Grüner Veltliner or Riesling.
Dürnstein is just along the bank, with the ruins of the castle where Richard the Lionheart was once held prisoner sitting high above the town. Further on, there's the great abbey at Melk.
It's a gentle trip… good food, good wine and no great distances, and just right for your autumn week.

item.title: Rosewood Phnom Penh (Wed 14 Oct)
item.description:
Destination Spotlight: if you're in Phnom Penh this autumn, there's a lovely little exhibition at the top of the Rosewood.
The hotel sits at the top of the Vattanac Capital Tower, looking out over the Tonlé Sap and the Mekong.
Up in the gallery on the 35th floor, the Cambodian artist Sothy Chhim is showing Heritage until the end of November. It's twenty works painted onto old rice sacks, with the stitching left showing, so every piece feels layered and a little worn in, in the nicest way.
We love finding something like this on a trip. Something you didn't plan for, that you end up thinking about all the way home.
If you're staying, it's yours to wander. Afterwards, there's a drink up at Sora as the city lights come on below.
Phnom Penh is a wonderful way into Cambodia, and we'd love to help you plan the rest.

item.title: Finnish Lapland (Thu 15 Oct)
item.description:
The dark evenings are back in Finnish Lapland, and with them, your chance of seeing the Northern Lights.
It's a lovely time to be here, with the colour fading on the fells and the first sharp edge in the air.
You spend the day out on the fells of Pallas-Yllästunturi National Park, perhaps passing a few reindeer on the way. Most of Lapland's 200,000 wander freely, so they tend to turn up when you least expect them.
Then it's back for a sauna, something warm to eat, and a long look at the sky.
The locals say there are eight seasons up here rather than four. This one might be our favourite.
If the Northern Lights have been on your mind, this is a gentle way to go looking for them.

item.title: Four Seasons Resort Peninsula Papagayo (Fri 16 Oct)
item.description:
Destination Spotlight: on a forested peninsula in Guanacaste, your mornings start on the water at Four Seasons Papagayo.
The resort looks out over Bahía de Culebra, so you can swim or kayak before breakfast and still have the whole day to yourself.
Even the Arnold Palmer golf course, winding through the forest above the bay, has just been recognised as an Audubon sanctuary for looking after the wildlife around it.
There's a new longevity programme too. The part we love is a journey out to the Nicoya Peninsula, one of the world's Blue Zones, where people are known for living long and well.
At the spa, there's a slow massage with warm bamboo, just what you want at the end of a warm day.
It's a beautiful first stop in Costa Rica, and one we think you'll love.

item.title: Megève (Sat 17 Oct)
item.description:
You can thank a baroness for Megève.
In the 1920s, Noémie de Rothschild fell for this little village in Haute-Savoie and decided France deserved its own answer to St Moritz. She built a hotel on Mont d'Arbois, laid out a golf course, and the rest followed.
A century on, it's kept all of that charm. Cobbled lanes, traditional chalets, a church tower in the middle of it all and little shops you'll want to take your time over.
We love it in autumn, before the skiers arrive. The high meadows turn golden, the forests go russet and the whole village feels like it's taking a deep breath.
Walk the high meadows in the morning, then come down for a long, cheesy lunch from the mountain larder.
And when winter comes, we can't wait to plan your return for the snow.
Come find us at No.82. 🕶️ ✉️ hello@agentnouveau.com

item.title: ⟡ A question we're often asked as summer fades
item.description:
⟡ A question we're often asked as summer fades
There's more sun left in the year than most people think.
Crete, Rhodes and Corfu keep their tavernas, hotels and shops open right through the year, no shutters, no waiting for April. Malta barely slows down either, its airport busier this year than last.
It's one of our favourite answers to give, to someone who thought they'd left it a little too late for sun.
There's a holiday that suits this stretch of the year too. Quieter beaches, a table free without booking weeks ahead, and evenings that stay warm long after the crowds have gone home.
Come in and tell us what kind of warm you're after. We'll point you at the right coastline.
Come find us at No.82.
🕶️ ✉️ hello@agentnouveau.com

item.title: ⟡ Some islands close the door completely for winter
item.description:
⟡ Some islands close the door completely for winter
Ios, Folegandros, Milos and Koufonisia do exactly that, hotels and tavernas closing their doors from late October and not opening again until spring.
There's something lovely about a place that simply stops for the season and means it.
It's a complete quiet, one you don't find anywhere else in the Mediterranean.
If that's the holiday you're after, the first half of October is your last real window this year. Worth booking sooner rather than later.
We're always happy to talk through timing over a drink, before you commit to a date.

item.title: ⟡ Two names above the door, and a story behind both
item.description:
⟡ Two names above the door, and a story behind both
You might arrive at a beautiful little hotel in Florence, somewhere tucked into the hills of Provence, or a place you've been dreaming about on a Greek island…… and notice another name sitting quietly alongside the hotel's own.
Leading Hotels of the World. Relais & Châteaux. They're names we've become so used to seeing that it's easy to skim past them. But they're worth noticing.
Ten hotels joined Leading Hotels of the World in August 2026, taking its collection beyond four hundred and fifty. Each one kept the name, personality and sense of place that made it special in the first place. The second name doesn't replace any of that. If anything, it tells you that somebody else noticed it too.
And getting there isn't easy. Both Leading Hotels of the World and Relais & Châteaux receive several hundred applications or enquiries each year, with only around thirty accepted.
Because the things that make a hotel truly lovely aren't always the things you can see online. It's how you're greeted when you arrive tired after a long journey. The breakfast that lingers into a slow morning. The person who remembers where you like to sit. The feeling that everything is being quietly looked after without you ever really noticing.
That little second name above the door tells you there are standards behind the scenes too. And when you're choosing somewhere to stay, that's exactly the kind of detail we love talking about.
Come and find us at No.82. 🖤 🕶️ ✉️ hello@agentnouveau.com

item.description:
⟡ The name that started on one beach
Sani began as one family's beach resort on Greece's Kassandra peninsula, back in 1970, long before anyone thought of it as a collection. When that same family wanted to take the same standard further afield, they built it under a different name, Ikos, instead of stretching the one they already had.
There's something rather lovely about a business that grows that way, keeping the original exactly where it started instead of folding everything into one big name.
We tell that one a lot at No.82. A name that started on one beach, and never forgot where it was.

item.title: ⟡ The part we like doing ourselves
item.description:
⟡ The part we like doing ourselves
A second name above a hotel's door tells you something real. Somebody with a reputation to look after has already been round that hotel and come away happy with it. Domes, the Greek group with resorts across Greece, Portugal and Spain, sits under Marriott's Autograph Collection and Luxury Collection too, with the Domes name kept exactly where it always was.
And then there's the part we love, which is all the rest of it. A beach you can walk for miles, or a little cove where the water barely moves. Music round the pool, or somewhere wonderfully still. A beautiful room you'll hardly be in, or a terrace you fully intend to disappear onto with a book.
Those things tell us far more about where you should stay than a logo does, and working them out with you is the bit we'd happily spend an hour on.

item.description:

It might be the least glamorous item on the whole shelf. It's also the one we'd argue hardest for.
It goes in before you've even thought about it, which is really the whole idea.

item.description:

item.description:

There's more sun left in the year than most people think.
Crete, Rhodes and Corfu keep their tavernas, hotels and shops open right through the year, no shutters, no waiting for April. Malta barely slows down either, its airport busier this year than last.

There's a holiday that suits this stretch of the year too. Quieter beaches, a table free without booking weeks ahead, and evenings that stay warm long after the crowds have gone home.

If that's the holiday you're after, the first half of October is your last real window this year. Worth booking sooner rather than later.

item.title: Gstaad (Fri 2 Oct)
item.description:
October is when we'd put you in Gstaad, and the promenade is why.
No cars anywhere near it, chalets either side, and the winter season still weeks off. The village sits at a thousand and fifty metres in the Saanenland, and they've been making cheese up here for something like a thousand years.
There's over three hundred kilometres of walking in the wider valley, and October is the month we'd do it in.
Then a long lunch, and a wander over to Saanen afterwards because it's only down the road.
It's the mountains without the lift queues, and you'll sleep beautifully. Send us a note when you're free and we'll find you the week.

item.title: Four Seasons Resort Bali at Sayan (Sat 3 Oct)
item.description:
Destination Spotlight: seven suites in Ubud reopened in July, rebuilt around the view you came for.
Four Seasons Resort Bali at Sayan has reworked seven of its suites, some of them over two floors, giving the family ones a room of their own for children rather than a made-over corner.
You come into a living room with the Ayung River valley filling the windows, then climb to a bedroom in teak and hand-loomed cloth.
Sayan has always been about that valley. Now the rooms are built around it.
You wake there with the river loud below you and the light coming up through the trees. Ubud is worth longer than you'd think, and we'll gladly help you plan the shape of it.
At Agent Nouveau, we build the holidays that put the view where you'll see it. 🖤

item.title: Brussels (Mon 5 Oct)
item.description:
We're dreaming of Brussels this morning, and of a narrow house you could walk straight past.
Number 266 Chaussée d'Haecht, in Schaerbeek, is where Victor Horta started. He built it in 1893 for his friend Eugène Autrique, an engineer at Solvay who wanted something comfortable and couldn't spend much on it.
It's a museum now, each room furnished as it would have been at the turn of the century, and you can watch a young architect working out what he was about to do to European architecture.
Given our name, you'll forgive us a soft spot for the man who started all this.
Brussels is about two hours from St Pancras, which makes it a lovely long weekend if you ask us about it.
At Agent Nouveau, we gather the half-days that make the whole trip. 🖤

item.title: The Oberoi Udaivilas (Tue 6 Oct)
item.description:
Destination Spotlight: thirty acres of garden on Lake Pichola, and you'd have a pool of your own in it.
You come into the Oberoi Udaivilas through domes and courtyards, with channels and reflecting pools threaded all through the grounds. Many of the eighty-seven rooms take their own pool off them.
In February they held the Concours d'Elegance here for a second year, and drove the cars along Fateh Sagar Lake so you could watch them move instead of stand.
Breakfast on your own terrace, with the lake getting on with its morning in front of you.
Give Udaipur three nights if you can. We'd happily build the rest of Rajasthan around it.
At Agent Nouveau, we look for the addresses you'd go out of your way for. 🖤

item.title: Lanzarote (Wed 7 Oct)
item.description:
César Manrique gave Lanzarote a look you can pick out from the air.
He was born in Arrecife in 1919, painted in Madrid and New York, and came home in the sixties to find the island filling with tower hotels. He spent the rest of his life arguing against them, and the height limits that followed are why you drive past low white villages instead.
Seven centres came out of all that. We'd start you at two of them. Jameos del Agua was the first, set down inside a collapsed lava tube. Mirador del Río is cut into the Famara cliff, and you come out at a window with El Río below you and La Graciosa across the water.
October's warm out there and the light goes long and low. You're always welcome at No.82 if you'd like a hand with where to stay.
At Agent Nouveau, we line up the winter escapes that kept their character. 🖤

item.title: Okanagan Valley (Thu 8 Oct)
item.description:
We're dreaming of British Columbia this morning. There's a wine valley out there we'd love to get you to.
Drive south out of Kelowna and you've the lake on one side and vines on the other. There are more than two hundred wineries down this valley and more than sixty grape varieties in the ground. Kelowna became Canada's first UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy in 2025.
Keep going and you reach Osoyoos, sitting in the only pocket desert in the country, where the lakes buffer the vines from the extremes.
Harvest runs through the autumn. Short drives, big lunches, early nights.
Perhaps an easier trip than you'd think, too, so do say if you fancy it for next autumn.
At Agent Nouveau, we bring together the road trips that earn the flight. 🖤

item.title: St. Regis Dubai, The Palm (Wed 23 Sep)
item.description:
Destination Spotlight: the St. Regis on Palm Jumeirah opens again on 1 November, ready for you.
It closed back in April for a full refurbishment. The restaurants at St. Regis Gardens carried on without it. That little stretch of the Palm has become a neighbourhood in its own right.
There are 264 rooms and 26 suites behind floor-to-ceiling glass, so you wake up looking at either the Gulf or the length of the Palm itself. Cordelia does breakfast indoors or out, and there's no hurry about any of it.
What we love about a reopening is that every small thing gets thought about again. The reading light. The coffee. Where you put your book down. If Dubai's on your mind for the winter, we'd love to hear about it.

item.title: Pena Palace (Thu 24 Sep)
item.description:
You can see it from half of Sintra, red and yellow on the ridge above the trees.
Ferdinand took a monastery that lightning and then the 1755 earthquake had finished off, and built a palace over the ruin between 1842 and 1854. He kept the cloister inside it. Gothic, Moorish, Renaissance, whatever he liked the look of, all on one building.
The colours faded over a century and were put back at the end of the last one, which is why it looks the way the paintings do again.
Walk down through the park afterwards, into the Countess's Garden, and the whole thing goes quiet within a minute.
Go early or go late. It's a short hop from Lisbon, and we'd give you the night in Sintra rather than the day trip.
At Agent Nouveau, we work out which hill you climb, and when. 🖤

item.title: The Langham, Custom House, Bangkok (Fri 25 Sep)
item.description:
Destination Spotlight: from 20 December you can have dinner in Bangkok's old Custom House.
It's stood on the Chao Phraya since 1888, drawn up by an Italian architect named Joachim Grassi, and spent its later years housing the river police and then fire-station families.
The Langham has taken its time bringing it back. The teak floors have stayed, along with the grand central staircase and the four-storey hallway you walk into before anyone's said a word to you. That building holds the restaurants and bars.
The sleeping happens next door, in a new one facing the water. Sixty rooms and fifteen suites.
If you've been to Bangkok and found it loud, this is the other half of the city. River light, old wood, and boats going past while you're still on your first coffee. Perhaps one for December. Let us know and we'll look.
At Agent Nouveau, we put together the trips that begin with one very good room. 🖤

item.title: Devon (Sat 26 Sep)
item.description:
There's a stretch of south Devon you'll recognise before you've ever set foot in it.
The Flete estate sits eleven miles east of Plymouth, and the stone house that played Barton Cottage in Sense and Sensibility is still standing on it. Newton Ferrers sits along the water from here.
There's a morning on Dartmoor in it, an afternoon poking about the villages, and a pub with a fire going, because by late September there usually is one.
Autumn suits it far better than August does, and the whole county slows down to meet you. Come and see us about the house, the pub and the timing.

item.title: Naoshima (Mon 28 Sep)
item.description:
We'd give you two nights on Naoshima rather than one.
It's a small island in the Seto Inland Sea, and Tadao Ando has been building there for decades. The newest of them, the Naoshima New Museum of Art, opened in May 2025, up on a hill above the old village at Honmura. It's three floors, and two of them are under the ground you're standing on. The art comes from across Asia.
Then you step back out into the afternoon, and there's the sea below you with a ferry crossing it.
That second evening is the one we'd stay for, with the light going down over the water.
Pop into No.82 and we'll build the rest of Japan around it.

item.title: Chiloé (Tue 29 Sep)
item.description:
You'll find churches on Chiloé that were put up by the men who built the boats.
Sixteen of the churches are World Heritage listed. They're native timber, and in place of iron nails they're pegged together with wood, the same way the islanders made their hulls. Another sixty-odd are scattered across the archipelago.
The oldest still standing is the church at Achao, Jesuit-built around 1730 and put back up in 1784 after a fire.
Imagine pushing the door open on a grey afternoon with the rain coming off the water. Inside it smells of wood, and the boards of the vault are bent across above you like a hull turned over.
It rains a good deal down there, and that's rather the point of the place.
Pair it with a few days further south, and we're glad to talk it through.
At Agent Nouveau, we piece together the weeks that take a bit of getting to. 🖤
